title: Paris 1719 code letters, BL Add MS 32305 ff. 6-7 (DECODE R2964, R2965)

plaintext.source: about a dozen interlinear glosses by the contemporary decipherer

transcription.notes: Counted with a bracket-aware script; the --measure tool also counts glosses as tokens.

system.summary: A two-part 3-figure code of about 900 groups mixing words, syllables and letters, in clear French letters.
system.notes: Two-part inferred from the contemporary glosses: re 36, pas 88, le 95, que 184, vous 243, a 347 are not alphabetical. The Carré letters of 1742-45 (R2968/R2970/R2972), filed here until 14 Oct 2026, are a different code: targets/carre1742.

prior_solution.where: contemporary interlinear glosses on R2964/R2965 (about a dozen values)

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: Fetched all images of R2963-R2974 with the DECODE cookie.
BL catalogue (unidentified cipher keys) and web search for the shelfmark; no edition.
Identified each record: R2963, R2966, R2967, R2971, R2973, R2974 deciphered at the time; R2969 a frequency count, not a key.
R2964 transcribed in full with the glosses.
354 groups, 191 distinct, 116 singletons, max 900; glosses not alphabetical, so a two-part code.
One-part (alphabetical) code, which would let the glosses bracket the rest.

Split under the one-key rule: the Carré letters (R2968, R2970, R2972), a different code, moved to carre1742 with the carre/ folder and its solver steps; this entry keeps the Paris 1719 code (R2964, R2965). The catalogue #79 records (R2978, R2979) and R2963/R2974, read at the time in other ciphers, are context only.

outcome.method_basis: The Paris 1719 letters are a two-part code; only the contemporary interlinear glosses on R2964/R2965 give values, and the code cannot be extended from about 700 groups.
outcome.notes: fraction_read counts the contemporary glosses in R2964 (33 of 354 groups). Needs a key, a clear copy or many more letters in the same code. The Carré letters were split off on 14 Oct 2026 to carre1742.

gaps.item: R2964 and R2965, the unglossed code groups (321 of 354 in f. 6; R2965 not transcribed)
gaps.detail: two-part code of ~900 entries, ~700 groups in all, no key, clear copy or other letter in the code
